## Amdahl's law for energy+min+removal (stages experiment)

f = (t_energy + t_min + t_removal) / t_total of the sequential run (the part that is parallel in this version). Limit = 1 / ((1 − f) + f / p): the speedup if the parallel part scaled perfectly and cost nothing extra.

## Fixed part vs per-seam work (sequential runs of main + main_nodp)

Seam k is computed on an image of width W − k, so the cost per seam shrinks during a run; the work of a run is P = H·(s·W − s(s−1)/2) pixel visits. Both models are fitted to the median t_total of each reduction (10/20/30 %; medians, so one slow run cannot move the line). Model 1: t_total = a + c·P (a = fixed part). Model 2 (naive): t_total = a′ + b·s; because the per-seam cost shrinks, its intercept a′ also contains per-seam work. Last column: the fixed part measured directly, t_total − Σ stage times (copy of the input, gray conversion, final crop). An intercept is only an extrapolation to zero seams: a 1 % change of the per-pixel cost between the reductions moves it by about 1 % of the run time.
